FSBTY1 Index.des_notes:

TTFGCY1 Index.name: Netherlands TTF Natural Gas Fo
TTFGCY1 Index.des_notes:
SECTOR DESCRIPTION: Physical Forward Prices for natural gas delivered to Virtual Trading Point Netherlands Title Transfer Facility (TTF). The Title Transfer Facility, more commonly known as TTF, is a virtual trading point for natural gas in the Netherlands. This trading point provides facility for a number of traders in Netherlands to trade futures, physical and exchange trades. Set up by Gasunie in 2003, it is almost identical to the National Balancing Point (NBP) in the United Kingdom and allows gas to be traded within the Dutch Gas network.

More information on TTF can be found here https://www.gasunietransportservices.nl/en/shippers/products-and-services/ttf

Product Specifications: Units: EUR/Mwh

Gas trades on a forward month,forward quarter,forward season or year forward basis.
Day-ahead = delivered next working day (Friday's Price reflects Monday delivery)
Weekend = delivered Saturday, Sunday
Week + 1 = delivered Monday-Friday of the front week
Months: All months are calendar months
Quarters: Q1 = January to March, Q2 = April to June, Q3 = July to September, Q4 = October to December
Seasonal contracts are as follows:
Summer - Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep;
Winter - Oct(Yr1), Nov(Yr1), Dec(Yr1), Jan(Yr2),Feb(Yr2),Mar(Yr2).
Calendar Year - Contracts are Jan-Dec. Gas Year contracts are Oct-Sep Close

SOURCE: Data comes from brokers/third parties. Please run {ALLQ} to see the sources pricing
this ticker.

UPDATE INFO: Energy broker pricing on Bloomberg updates on a near real-time basis. It is
important to note that updates only occur when there is activity in the market, so there may not be
updates on every contract every day.

SOURCE METHODOLOGY: N/A

HISTORICAL CONSIDERATIONS: N/A

DATA DISCOVERY: Generic contracts run continuously and link the underlying specific contracts.
Generics are rolled in order to maintain the correct reference forward contract. For example,
{TTFG1MON Index DES} represents the first month forward.

Specific contracts can be found by running 'TTFG' followed by M (Month), Q (Quarter), S (Season)
or Y (Year).
For example:
{TTFGM F15 Index DES} - Jan 2015
{TTFGQ Q115 Index DES} - Q1 2015
{TTFGS SU15 Index DES} - Summer 2015
{TTFGS WI1516 Index DES} - Winter 2015/16
{TTFGY 15 Index DES} - Year 2015
The month contract codes are:
Jan-F Feb-G Mar-H Apr-J May-K Jun-M Jul-N Aug-Q Sep-U Oct-V Nov-X Dec-Z

RELATED SECTORS/FUNCTIONS:
{ALLX GPTT } - German GPL/ Dutch TTF Hi Cal Natural Gas Forward Prices
{ALLX EGTF } - Natural Gas Forward German NCG/ Dutch TTF Hi Cal Forward Prices

USE AS A FINANCIAL BENCHMARK MAY BE RESTRICTED. SEE {DOCS #2084680}

PRIB03M Index.name: Czech Interbank Offered Rates
PRIB03M Index.des_notes:
Czech Interbank Offered Rates 1 Month PRIBOR (or Prague Interbank Offered Rate) is the average interest rate at which unsecured CZK funds are offered by Panel Banks in the interbank market, just prior to 11.00am local time. The calculation of PRIBOR shall take place at 11:00am Prague local time. Individual Panel Bank contributions shall be published at 15:00. Relevant documentation may be found at: https://cfbf.cz/pribor/governance-oversight/code-of-conduct/ and https://cfbf.cz/pribor/

Real-time PRIBOR data is fee-liable. Non-subscribers receive 24-hour delayed data on Terminal. From 1st Jan 2026, a CFBF license is required for delayed Data License access. Non-subscribers will lose access over DL 16th June 2026. Contact subscriptions@cfbf.cz for licensing. Real-time users require EID 74556 . Delayed Data License users require EID 100499.

CZRUSHIN Index.name: Czech Republic Rushin Weekly E
CZRUSHIN Index.des_notes: This concept provides an estimate of overall economic activity in an economy. It is typically a monthly measure of value added by industry (sometimes referred to as monthly GDP) that is released in advance of quarterly GDP estimates. The Rushin Index tracks the real-time dynamics of the Czech GDP on a weekly basis. It combines alternative high-frequency indicators with standard low-frequency macroeconomic data. The index, capturing q-o-q GDP growth in per cent, is developed and maintained by the Czech National Bank.
